first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are funnel-mechanics problems, and memory_86 plus memory_31 and memory_91 all point at that cluster. The competitor's entry pricing is the loudest signal, but responding to it with promotional_pricing is the option most likely to buy short-term acquisition at the cost of the stated objective: discount-acquired SMB cohorts tend to anchor on price, compress margin, and churn faster, so 'revenue lift' in a consolidated summary can mask negative long-term qualified revenue. That is exactly why memory_73 is my first verification pull: it is the broadest, most flattering claim in the inherited set ('strong acquisition and revenue lift', 'cut time-to-first-value', 'held across both billing plans'), and claims that survive consolidation with no caveats are the ones most likely to have lost their caveats. I want the original record's margin, retention, and time-horizon detail before I let it drive a pricing move. Second pull is memory_86, because it is the memory I actually intend to act on and I need to know whether 'shortening onboarding' improved completion by removing friction or by removing qualification steps -- the latter would lift the metric while degrading downstream lead quality, the same failure mode that makes memory_31's field-cutting result worth treating as provisional. If verification shows memory_86's lift came from removing genuine friction, I run the onboarding experiment at standard scale with a holdout and downstream qualified-revenue tracking, not just completion rate. If it shows qualification steps were stripped, I fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91), which improves engagement without touching the qualification gate. If memory_73 comes back genuinely clean on margin and retention, promotional pricing becomes a defensible second slot next week, but I would still not spend the only slot this week on the option whose upside is most likely to be an artifact of lossy summarization. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is real but addresses neither current decline and does not answer the SMB pressure. All inherited claims here are summaries, not evidence; I am treating them as leads with decaying reliability rather than settled facts.
